content.content:
1	YOUR TASK: write, from scratch, the weights of a transformer that reads the log of an AI coding agent's session and, at every event, classifies the agent's recent behaviour into one of four classes, as well as possible. There is no training: no data, no labels, no loss, no gradients, no fine-tuning; you choose every number yourself. You have no tools: no code execution, no calculator, nothing to run, no files to read; everything you are given is in this message. You will get no feedback: nothing is run, and the network is scored only after you have finished. You may take as many replies as you need. After each reply you will receive only the message "Continue." (it carries no feedback, and nothing is run in between); after a reply that was cut off by a length limit you may instead receive a fixed notice that it was cut off. If a reply is cut off, continue in your next reply; if the cut fell inside an edits block, open a new edits block and write the cut statement again in full. Every edits block in every reply is read and applied, in the order written. First describe your design briefly (the strategy, and what the attention heads and MLP units compute), then write the edits blocks. End your final reply with a line that is exactly END OF WEIGHTS (outside any edits block).
2	
3	THE TASK: an AI coding agent works through a session of tool calls (reading and editing files, searching, running tests, builds and lints, HTTP calls, polling, planning). Its session log is rendered as text, one event block per tool call, and tokenised. At every event, your network classifies the pattern of the agent's most recent eight operations into one of four classes. The sessions are synthetic: a simulator generates them, and an oracle labels each window from the simulator's hidden state. The task's specification follows; its section numbers are kept, so a reference such as §4.3 points to that section of the specification.
4	
5	## 1. Objective
6	
7	At every event of an AI coding agent's session, the model classifies the pattern of the agent's most recent eight operations as one of four classes:
8	
9	1. **PRODUCTIVE**: evidence of forward progress or materially new investigation.
10	2. **RECOVERY**: a bounded retry or repair after a transient or diagnosed failure, still within policy or recently resolved.
11	3. **STALLED**: repeated ineffective operations, with no observed progress and no state-reversion cycle.
12	4. **OSCILLATING**: recurring reversal between previously held workspace or execution states, with no net progress.
13	
14	The model reads the session's rendered log. No hand-written feature extractor sits between the log and the network. There is only a fixed renderer (§4) and a fixed tokeniser (§5).
15	
16	### 1.2 What a good result does and does not show
17	
18	- **The logs are synthetic, in one fixed grammar.** There is one header line per tool call, with a family-specific tool name and canonical result syntax. Tool output and assistant text are absent, and diff content is replaced by opaque hunk ids. A good score shows hand-programmed perception over this grammar. It does not show robustness to real transcripts.
19	- **Segmentation is given, not perceived.** `EOE` tokens, the `event_ord` input and an attention bias indexed by event distance make "same event" and "within the last 8 events" one scalar table each. This mirrors transcripts where each tool call is a record. It is a task-aligned inductive bias, and it computes no content signal.
20	- **The tokeniser is fixed and word-level.** Paths and identifiers are single tokens, and numbers are digit groups. It computes no repeat, state or delta signal.
21	- **Diff hunks are opaque ids.** Whether an edit repeats, undoes or restores an earlier change is visible. Whether it is correct code is not. In the real world, progress shows only through later validation, and that is the case here too.
22	- v0.3 makes no claim that hand-programming beats training.
23	
24	## 6. Windows, gate, labels
25	
26	- **Oracle rules.** The labels come from the v0.2 oracle. Its §6.1–§6.3 (latent state definitions, parameters, rules) and the family names in its §7.1 follow.
27	- **Gate rule.** Windows with withheld observations are not scored.
28	
29	## v0.2 oracle rules and scenario families (unchanged in v0.3)
30	
31	The labels are produced by the v0.2 oracle from the simulator's latent state. Its definitions,
32	parameters and rules (v0.2 §6.1-§6.3) and the names of the scenario families (v0.2 §7.1) are
33	reproduced here. "Encoded features" and "the 120-vector" refer to v0.2's input, which v0.3
34	replaces with the rendered log.
35	
36	#### 6.1 Latent state (simulator-internal, never encoded)
37	
38	Per session the simulator maintains:
39	
40	- `progress p_t ∈ [0, 1]`: hidden objective completion.
41	- `knowledge K_t`: a set of latent facts about the fault. An operation may add facts. A new fact is "material narrowing".
42	- `workspace W_t`: real simulated file contents. Digests are computed from these.
43	- `episodes`: failure episodes with latent cause (`transient`, `persistent`, `diagnosed_repair`), a retry counter and a resolution flag.
44	- Per-operation latent effect: one of `PROGRESS`, `NEW_FACT`, `RESOLVES_EPISODE`, `IN_POLICY_RETRY`, `IN_POLICY_POLL`, `REVERSION`, `REDUNDANT`, `NONE`.
45	
46	`REDUNDANT` means the operation repeats work already reflected in latent state. It re-acquires a fact already in `K_t`, re-applies an edit already present in `W_t`, re-runs validation on an unchanged workspace, or is an out-of-policy retry or poll. Redundancy is defined against `K_t` and `W_t`, **not** against `intent_fingerprint`, so it stays independent of the encoded features. `NONE` means the operation is novel but yielded nothing, for example a first read of a file that turns out to be irrelevant.
47	
48	An episode's **initial failing operation** has effect `NONE`, because the attempt itself was reasonable. Its in-policy retries are `IN_POLICY_RETRY`. Retries beyond `R_max` are `REDUNDANT`.
49	
50	An operation is **stall-ineffective** iff its latent effect is `REDUNDANT` or `REVERSION`. An operation is **ineffective** iff it is stall-ineffective or has effect `NONE`.
51	
52	A **reversion** is an agent mutation whose latent after-state equals a workspace state held earlier in the window **and** that undoes an earlier agent mutation. External resets don't count.
53	
54	#### 6.2 Pre-registered oracle parameters
55	
56	| Symbol | Value | Meaning |
57	|---|---:|---|
58	| `ε_p` | 0.02 | Progress tolerance over a window |
59	| `F_prod` | 2 | Minimum new facts in the window for investigative PRODUCTIVE |
60	| `N_stall` | 5 | Minimum ineffective operations of 8 for STALLED |
61	| `N_grey` | 3 | Lower bound of the stall grey zone |
62	| `N_rev` | 2 | Minimum reversions in the window for OSCILLATING |
63	| `R_max` | 3 | Maximum retries of one intent within an episode while still in policy |
64	| `P_max` | 5 | Maximum polls of an external dependency (with backoff) while still in policy |
65	| `k_rec` | 4 | Recency horizon for RECOVERY |
66	
67	#### 6.3 Window labelling rules (evaluated in order; first match wins)
68	
69	Let `Δp` be the progress change across the window, `F` the number of new facts, `I` the number of **stall-ineffective** operations (`REDUNDANT` + `REVERSION`) and `V` the number of reversions.
70	
71	1. **INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (instrumentation):** the generator deliberately dropped a required observation (scenario 12).
72	2. **OSCILLATING:** `V ≥ N_rev` and `Δp ≤ ε_p`.
73	3. **STALLED:** `Δp ≤ ε_p`, `F = 0`, `I ≥ N_stall`, the final event is stall-ineffective, **and** no episode is in policy at the endpoint.
74	4. **RECOVERY:** an episode is active at the endpoint with retries ≤ `R_max` (or polls ≤ `P_max`), **or** an episode resolved within the last `k_rec` events.
75	5. **PRODUCTIVE:** `Δp > ε_p` or `F ≥ F_prod`.
76	6. **INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (ambiguous):** everything else. This includes the grey zone `N_grey ≤ I < N_stall` with no progress, windows with a single new fact and no progress, and aimless novel activity (mostly `NONE` effects). Novel but fruitless exploration is never labelled STALLED. Repetition of already-done work is what defines a stall.
77	
78	This ordering gives `OSCILLATING > STALLED > RECOVERY > PRODUCTIVE`. The recency bound in rule 4 stops a long-resolved retry from overriding later productive work.
79	
80	Labels depend on latent causal state. Observable features are emitted independently by the event layer. Labels are never defined in terms of encoded features. For example, there must be no rule of the form "STALLED iff `repeated_intent`".
81	
82	#### 7.1 Scenario families (names only)
83	
84	1. Incremental productive repair: failing tests, targeted edits, fewer failures, eventually green.
85	2. Productive exploration: several inspections and diagnostics before a meaningful change.
86	3. Transient external failure: repeated timeout, then success, then productive work.
87	4. Bounded backoff or retry: a recoverable failure with one or two controlled retries.
88	5. Repeated failed test invocation with unchanged artefact and unchanged failure.
89	6. Repeated edits that change files but don't improve validation.
90	7. A/B/A/B workspace oscillation between competing edits.
91	8. Tool oscillation: two operations repeatedly undo each other's effects.
92	9. Benign lookalike: repeated test runs with genuine incremental improvement.
93	10. Benign lookalike: repeated reads or polls while an external dependency legitimately recovers.
94	11. Rising context or token expenditure without useful work. Cost is weak supporting evidence, not a label shortcut.
95	12. Under-instrumented sessions, for gate coverage.
96	
97	THE LOGS (the network's input): each session is rendered by renderer.py into one text block per event and tokenised by tokenizer.py (encode_session); the network reads the token ids, with each token's event ordinal and offset. Below: the specification's rendering and tokeniser sections, the id of every fixed token, the records the renderer reads, the exact source of renderer.py and tokenizer.py, and a grammar sheet with one invented example block per tool and its tokens.
98	
99	## 4. Log rendering (frozen)
100	
101	### 4.1 Layout
102	
103	The log is `BOS`, then one **event block** per event in order. Each block is a header line plus up to 6 body lines, all ASCII (non-ASCII characters become `?` before any marker is inserted). The truncation marker is the ASCII word `TRUNC`.
104	
105	### 4.2 Header line
106	
107	```
108	{HH:MM:SS.mmm} {tool} {fields…} -> {status} in={input_tokens} out={output_tokens}
109	```
110	
111	| Tool | Fields (budget in tokens) | Status |
112	|---|---|---|
113	| `read_file` | `path={p}` [`lines={a}-{b}`] | `ok` / `error` |
114	| `search` | `scope={s} query="{q}"` (query ≤ 12) [`limit={n}`] | `ok` |
115	| `list_dir` | `path={p}` | `ok` |
116	| `edit_file` | `path={p}` | `ok` / `error` |
117	| `write_file` | `path={p}` | `ok` / `error` |
118	| `revert` | `paths={p1},{p2}…` (≤ 16) | `ok` |
119	| `run_tests` | `suite={s}` [`tests={t1},{t2}…`] (≤ 24) | `ok` or `FAILED` |
120	| `build`, `lint` | `target={t}` (`?` if the suite was dropped) | `ok` or `FAILED` |
121	| `http_call` | `{METHOD} https://{host}{path_template}` [`body={json}`] (body ≤ 16) `req={hex8}` | `ok` / `error` |
122	| `poll_status` | `resource={r}` [`backoff={b}`] | `ready` / `pending` |
123	| `plan`, `ask`, `yield` | `action={action_type}` | `ok` |
124	
125	- **Validation counts.** For any event with a validation result, the status is followed by `{passed}/{total} passed`.
126	- **Field budgets.** A field over its budget is cut and ends with `TRUNC`.
127	- **The suffix is never cut.** The suffix is `-> {status} … in= out=`.
128	- **Header limit.** The whole header is at most 64 tokens, `TRUNC` included.
129	
130	### 4.3 Body lines
131	
132	These are emitted in this order, at most 6 lines in total:
133	
134	1. **Hunk lines.** One line per changed file, in path order:
135	   ```
136	     @ {path} {h_old} > {h_new}
137	   ```
138	   - The diff is `difflib.unified_diff(before.split("\n"), after.split("\n"), n=0)`.
139	   - `h_x` is `h` plus the first 10 hex characters of `sha256(session_id + ":hunk:" + path + ":" + text)`, where `text` is the file's removed lines (for `h_old`) or added lines (for `h_new`), taken across all hunks in diff order and joined with `\n`.
140	   - An empty side renders as `h0`.
141	   - The same change in the same file and session always gets the same ids. An undo swaps them, and a return to earlier content reuses an earlier id.
142	   - The number of hunks inside a file is not shown. At most `min(5, 6 − tail lines)` file lines are shown. If more files changed, the last shown line is `  @ TRUNC {k}`, where `k` is the number of files not shown.
143	   - Hunk lines are still shown when workspace digests were dropped. Those windows are not scored, but later windows may refer back to them.
144	2. **Error line** (ERROR outcome only):
145	   ```
146	     ! {error_class} at {error_location}:{line} ({noise})
147	   ```
148	   - `{line}` is `int(sha256(session_id+":"+error_location)[:4],16) % 900 + 1`, so it is stable across repeats.
149	   - `{noise}` is `pid {n}` or `0x{hex8}`, drawn from the event's render RNG.
150	3. **Workspace line** (`[workspace untracked]`), emitted when either digest was dropped.
151	
152	### 4.4 Missing observations
153	
154	Each dropped field renders as `?` in its own position, for example `in=? out=812`, `?/18 passed`, `suite=?`, or `! ? at ?:? (…)` when the failure was dropped.
155	
156	### 4.5 Noise
157	
158	- **Render RNG.** Each event has its own render RNG, `random.Random(int(sha256(canonical_json(RawOp) + ":render")[:16], 16))`. It supplies `req=` and `{noise}`. It is independent of the generators and the oracle.
159	- **Timestamps.** These are parsed with `datetime.fromisoformat` and rendered in UTC as `HH:MM:SS.mmm`.
160	
161	### 4.6 Bound
162	
163	A block has at most 64 header tokens, then for each of up to 6 body lines one line-marker token plus at most 20 tokens, then `EOE`. That is at most 64 + 6·21 + 1 = 191 < `O`. The renderer enforces the per-line cap with `TRUNC`.
164	
165	## 5. Tokeniser (frozen)
166	
167	A deterministic left-to-right scan of each block. Spaces and tabs are dropped.
168	
169	| Rule | Token |
170	|---|---|
171	| A newline followed (after spaces) by `@`, `!` or `[` | one reserved line-marker id `NL@`, `NL!` or `NL[` (the character is consumed) |
172	| Any other newline | `NL` |
173	| `WORD = [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.\-/]*` | one token: a reserved id if the word is reserved, otherwise a hashed id |
174	| `NUM = [0-9]+` | split left to right into groups of 3 digits (the last group may be shorter); each group is a dedicated id |
175	| Any other printable character | one punctuation id |
176	
177	**Vocabulary (V = 10,240):**
178	
179	| Ids | Content |
180	|---|---|
181	| 0 | `PAD` |
182	| 1 | `BOS` |
183	| 2 | `EOE` |
184	| 3 | `NL` |
185	| 4–6 | `NL@`, `NL!`, `NL[` |
186	| 7–127 | reserved words, frozen in `tokenizer.py`: all tool names; the words `path lines scope query limit bytes paths suite tests target body req resource backoff action in out ok error FAILED passed ready pending at pid workspace untracked TRUNC https GET POST PUT PATCH DELETE` |
187	| 128–223 | printable ASCII punctuation |
188	| 224–1,333 | digit groups `0`–`9`, `00`–`99`, `000`–`999` |
189	| 1,334–2,047 | unused |
190	| 2,048–10,239 | other words: `2048 + int(sha256(word)[:8],16) mod 8192` |
191	
192	The tokeniser returns `tokens`, `event_ord`, `offset`, the indices of the `EOE` tokens, and the **surface strings** (each token's text before hashing).
193	
194	Token ids (the tables of tokenizer.py, listed):
195	Special and line-marker tokens:
196	  0 PAD (padding only; never produced)   1 BOS   2 EOE   3 NL   4 NL@   5 NL!   6 NL[
197	Reserved words (ids 7-54; ids 55-127 are never produced):
198	  7 read_file   8 search   9 list_dir   10 edit_file   11 write_file   12 revert   13 run_tests
199	  14 build   15 lint   16 http_call   17 poll_status   18 plan   19 ask   20 yield
200	  21 path   22 lines   23 scope   24 query   25 limit   26 bytes   27 paths
201	  28 suite   29 tests   30 target   31 body   32 req   33 resource   34 backoff
202	  35 action   36 in   37 out   38 ok   39 error   40 FAILED   41 passed
203	  42 ready   43 pending   44 at   45 pid   46 workspace   47 untracked   48 TRUNC
204	  49 https   50 GET   51 POST   52 PUT   53 PATCH   54 DELETE
205	Punctuation (ids 128-158; ids 159-223 are never produced):
206	  128 !   129 "   130 #   131 $   132 %   133 &   134 '   135 (
207	  136 )   137 *   138 +   139 ,   140 -   141 .   142 /   143 :
208	  144 ;   145 <   146 =   147 >   148 ?   149 @   150 [   151 \
209	  152 ]   153 ^   154 `   155 {   156 |   157 }   158 ~
210	Digit groups (a number is split left to right into groups of 3 digits; the last group may be shorter):
211	  a 1-digit group g ("0".."9") has id 224 + g (224-233); a 2-digit group ("00".."99") has id 234 + its value
212	  (234-333); a 3-digit group ("000".."999") has id 334 + its value (334-1333). For example "09" is 243 and
213	  "250" is 584. Ids 1334-2047 are never produced.
214	Every other word: id 2048 + (int(sha256(word)[:8], 16) mod 8192), in 2048-10239.
215	
216	## Operation records (`RawOp` dicts, the renderer's input)
217	
218	`renderer.render_session(ops, session_id)` returns one block string per operation; `ops` is a list
219	of plain dicts, one per tool call, with these keys (a missing key reads as null; `session_id` is any
220	string, and it seeds the hunk ids and error line numbers of §4.3):
221	
222	| Key | Type | Meaning |
223	|---|---|---|
224	| `family` | str | The tool name: `read_file`, `search`, `list_dir`, `edit_file`, `write_file`, `revert`, `run_tests`, `build`, `lint`, `http_call`, `poll_status`, `plan`, `ask`, `yield` |
225	| `target` | str, list or dict | What the call acts on: the path (`read_file`, `list_dir`, `edit_file`, `write_file`), the scope (`search`), the list of paths (`revert`), the suite (`run_tests`), the target (`build`, `lint`), `{"method", "host", "path_template"}` (`http_call`), the resource (`poll_status`) |

289	def _fit(text: str, budget: int) -> str:

291

413	def _header(op: Any, rng: random.Random) -> str:
414	    head = f"{_clock(_get(op, 'timestamp'))} {_get(op, 'family')}"
415	    suffix = _status(op)
416	    fields = _ascii(_fields(op, rng))
417	    room = HEADER_MAX_TOKENS - _ntok(head) - _ntok(suffix)

427	def render_event(op: Any, session_id: str) -> str:
428	    rng = render_rng(op)
429	    header = _header(op, rng)
430	    hunk_lines: list[str] = []
431	    for ch in sorted(_get(op, "changed") or [], key=lambda c: c["path"]):
432	        # One line per changed file (spec v0.3 r2 §4.3): all removed lines vs all added lines of the
433	        # n=0 diff, so the number of hunks inside a file is not shown.
434	        hunks = diff_hunks(ch.get("before"), ch.get("after"))
435	        if not hunks:
436	            continue
437	        removed = [ln for r, _ in hunks for ln in r]
438	        added = [ln for _, a in hunks for ln in a]
439	        path = ch["path"]
440	        hunk_lines.append(f"{path} {hunk_id(session_id, path, removed)} > {hunk_id(session_id, path, added)}")
441	    tail: list[str] = []
442	    if _get(op, "outcome") == "ERROR":
443	        dropped = set(_get(op, "dropped") or ())
444	        loc = _get(op, "error_location")
445	        if "failure" in dropped:
446	            cls, loc_s, line = "?", "?", "?"
447	        else:
448	            cls = _q(_get(op, "error_class"))
449	            loc_s = _q(loc)
450	            line = "?" if loc is None else str(int(hashlib.sha256(f"{session_id}:{loc}".encode()).hexdigest()[:4], 16) % 900 + 1)
451	        noise = f"pid {rng.randint(1000, 99999)}" if rng.random() < 0.5 else f"0x{rng.getrandbits(32):08x}"
452	        tail.append(("!", f"{cls} at {loc_s}:{line} ({noise})"))
453	    if set(_get(op, "dropped") or ()) & set(DIGEST_DROPS):
454	        tail.append(("[", "workspace untracked]"))
455	    max_hunks = min(HUNK_MAX_LINES, BODY_MAX_LINES - len(tail))
456	    if len(hunk_lines) > max_hunks:
457	        omitted = len(hunk_lines) - (max_hunks - 1)
458	        hunk_lines = hunk_lines[: max_hunks - 1] + [f"{TRUNC} {omitted}"]
459	    body = [_line("@", h) for h in hunk_lines] + [_line(m, t) for m, t in tail]
460	    return "\n".join([header] + body)
461	
462	
463	def render_session(rawops: Sequence[Any], session_id: str) -> list[str]:
464	    return [render_event(op, session_id) for op in rawops]

469	```python
470	"""v0.3 tokeniser (spec v0.3 §5). Frozen; ships in the authoring packet.
471	
472	Standalone: standard library only, no relative imports.
473	
474	    enc = encode_session(blocks)   # blocks: one rendered string per event (renderer.render_session)
475	    enc.tokens, enc.event_ord, enc.offset, enc.eoe_index, enc.surface
476	
477	A session is ``BOS`` followed, for each event block, by the block's tokens and then ``EOE``.
478	``event_ord`` is 0 for ``BOS`` and k+1 for every token of block k, including its ``EOE``.
479	``offset`` is the 0-based position within the block (``BOS`` has offset 0); an offset >= ``O`` raises.
480	"""
481	
482	from __future__ import annotations
483	
484	import hashlib
485	import re
486	from dataclasses import dataclass
487	
488	V = 10240
489	O = 192
490	
491	PAD, BOS, EOE, NL = 0, 1, 2, 3
492	NL_AT, NL_BANG, NL_BRACKET = 4, 5, 6
493	LINE_MARKERS = {"@": NL_AT, "!": NL_BANG, "[": NL_BRACKET}
494	
495	TOOL_NAMES = (
496	    "read_file", "search", "list_dir", "edit_file", "write_file", "revert", "run_tests", "build", "lint",
497	    "http_call", "poll_status", "plan", "ask", "yield",
498	)
499	FIELD_AND_STATUS_WORDS = (
500	    "path", "lines", "scope", "query", "limit", "bytes", "paths", "suite", "tests", "target", "body", "req",
501	    "resource", "backoff", "action", "in", "out", "ok", "error", "FAILED", "passed", "ready", "pending", "at",
502	    "pid", "workspace", "untracked", "TRUNC", "https", "GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE",
503	)
504	RESERVED_WORDS: tuple[str, ...] = TOOL_NAMES + FIELD_AND_STATUS_WORDS
505	RESERVED_BASE = 7
506	assert RESERVED_BASE + len(RESERVED_WORDS) <= 128
507	RESERVED_IDS: dict[str, int] = {w: RESERVED_BASE + i for i, w in enumerate(RESERVED_WORDS)}
508	
509	PUNCT_BASE = 128
510	PUNCT_CHARS = "".join(chr(c) for c in range(33, 127) if not chr(c).isalnum() and chr(c) != "_")
511	assert len(PUNCT_CHARS) <= 96
512	PUNCT_IDS: dict[str, int] = {ch: PUNCT_BASE + i for i, ch in enumerate(PUNCT_CHARS)}
513	
514	DIGIT_BASE = 224
515	DIGIT_GROUPS: tuple[str, ...] = (
516	    tuple(f"{i}" for i in range(10)) + tuple(f"{i:02d}" for i in range(100)) + tuple(f"{i:03d}" for i in range(1000))
517	)
518	DIGIT_IDS: dict[str, int] = {g: DIGIT_BASE + i for i, g in enumerate(DIGIT_GROUPS)}
519	assert DIGIT_BASE + len(DIGIT_GROUPS) == 1334
520	
521	HASH_BASE = 2048
522	HASH_BUCKETS = 8192
523	assert HASH_BASE + HASH_BUCKETS == V
524	
525	_WORD = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.\-/]*")
526	_NUM = re.compile(r"[0-9]+")
527	
528	
529	class TokenizerError(ValueError):
530	    pass
531	
532	
533	def word_id(word: str) -> int:
534	    """Id of a WORD token: reserved id if reserved, otherwise its hashed bucket."""
535	    if word in RESERVED_IDS:
536	        return RESERVED_IDS[word]
537	    return HASH_BASE + int(hashlib.sha256(word.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8], 16) % HASH_BUCKETS
538	
539	
540	def digit_groups(num: str) -> list[str]:
541	    """Split a digit string left to right into groups of 3 (the last may be shorter)."""
542	    return [num[i : i + 3] for i in range(0, len(num), 3)]
543	
544	
545	def tokenize_spans(block: str) -> list[tuple[int, str, int, int]]:
546	    """(id, surface, start, end) per token of one event block (without EOE); ``block[start:end]`` is the
547	    matched source text (for a line marker, the newline, any spaces and the marker character)."""
548	    out: list[tuple[int, str, int, int]] = []
549	    i, n = 0, len(block)
550	    while i < n:
551	        ch = block[i]
552	        if ch in " \t":
553	            i += 1
554	            continue
555	        if ch == "\n":
556	            j = i + 1
557	            while j < n and block[j] in " \t":
558	                j += 1
559	            if j < n and block[j] in LINE_MARKERS:
560	                out.append((LINE_MARKERS[block[j]], "\n" + block[j], i, j + 1))
561	                i = j + 1
562	            else:
563	                out.append((NL, "\n", i, i + 1))
564	                i += 1
565	            continue
566	        m = _WORD.match(block, i)
567	        if m:
568	            w = m.group(0)
569	            out.append((word_id(w), w, i, m.end()))
570	            i = m.end()
571	            continue
572	        m = _NUM.match(block, i)
573	        if m:
574	            for k, g in enumerate(digit_groups(m.group(0))):
575	                out.append((DIGIT_IDS[g], g, i + 3 * k, i + 3 * k + len(g)))
576	            i = m.end()
577	            continue
578	        if ch in PUNCT_IDS:
579	            out.append((PUNCT_IDS[ch], ch, i, i + 1))
580	            i += 1
581	            continue
582	        raise TokenizerError(f"unrenderable character {ch!r} at {i}")
583	    return out
584	
585	
586	def tokenize_block(block: str) -> list[tuple[int, str]]:
587	    """(id, surface) pairs for one event block (without EOE)."""
588	    return [(tid, s) for tid, s, _, _ in tokenize_spans(block)]
589	
590	
591	@dataclass(frozen=True)
592	class Encoded:
593	    tokens: list[int]
594	    event_ord: list[int]
595	    offset: list[int]
596	    eoe_index: list[int]
597	    surface: list[str]
598	
599	
600	def encode_session(blocks: list[str]) -> Encoded:
601	    tokens, event_ord, offset, eoe, surface = [BOS], [0], [0], [], ["<BOS>"]
602	    for k, block in enumerate(blocks):
603	        pairs = tokenize_block(block)
604	        pairs.append((EOE, "<EOE>"))
605	        if len(pairs) > O:
606	            raise TokenizerError(f"event block {k} has {len(pairs)} tokens (offset >= O={O})")
607	        for off, (tid, s) in enumerate(pairs):
608	            tokens.append(tid)
609	            event_ord.append(k + 1)
610	            offset.append(off)
611	            surface.append(s)
612	        eoe.append(len(tokens) - 1)
613	    return Encoded(tokens, event_ord, offset, eoe, surface)
614	
615	
616	def prefix(enc: Encoded, t: int) -> Encoded:
617	    """The encoding of blocks 0..t (inclusive): a prefix ending at EOE_t."""
618	    end = enc.eoe_index[t] + 1
619	    return Encoded(enc.tokens[:end], enc.event_ord[:end], enc.offset[:end], enc.eoe_index[: t + 1], enc.surface[:end])
620	```

622	# Grammar sheet (spec v0.3 §4-§5)
623	
624	Each example below is one **event block** as the frozen renderer lays it out, followed by its
625	tokens from the frozen tokenizer (`tokenizer.tokenize_block`, then `EOE`), one per line as
626	`offset  id  surface`. Line-marker tokens are shown as `NL@`, `NL!` and `NL[`.
627	
628	Every path, suite, test, target, host, action, error class, hunk id and number here is
629	**invented** for illustration. Real logs use the same grammar with other values.
630	
631	A session is `BOS` followed by its blocks in order (`tokenizer.encode_session`). `event_ord` is 0
632	for `BOS` and k+1 for every token of block k, including its `EOE`; `offset` restarts at 0 in every
633	block. The network's prediction for block k is read at that block's `EOE`.
634	
635	Header suffix: `-> {status}[ {passed}/{total} passed] in={input_tokens} out={output_tokens}`.
636	Body lines, at most 6, in this order: hunk lines (`@`, at most 5), the error line (`!`, ERROR
637	outcomes only) and the workspace line (`[`, when a digest was dropped). A dropped observation is
638	rendered as `?` in its own position.

YOUR TASK: write, from scratch, the weights of a transformer that reads the log of an AI coding agent's session and, at every event, classifies the agent's recent behaviour into one of four classes, as well as possible. There is no training: no data, no labels, no loss, no gradients, no fine-tuning; you choose every number yourself. You have no tools: no code execution, no calculator, nothing to run, no files to read; everything you are given is in this message. You will get no feedback: nothing is run, and the network is scored only after you have finished. You may take as many replies as you need. After each reply you will receive only the message "Continue." (it carries no feedback, and nothing is run in between); after a reply that was cut off by a length limit you may instead receive a fixed notice that it was cut off. If a reply is cut off, continue in your next reply; if the cut fell inside an edits block, open a new edits block and write the cut statement again in full. Every edits block in every reply is read and applied, in the order written. First describe your design briefly (the strategy, and what the attention heads and MLP units compute), then write the edits blocks. End your final reply with a line that is exactly END OF WEIGHTS (outside any edits block).

THE TASK: an AI coding agent works through a session of tool calls (reading and editing files, searching, running tests, builds and lints, HTTP calls, polling, planning). Its session log is rendered as text, one event block per tool call, and tokenised. At every event, your network classifies the pattern of the agent's most recent eight operations into one of four classes. The sessions are synthetic: a simulator generates them, and an oracle labels each window from the simulator's hidden state. The task's specification follows; its section numbers are kept, so a reference such as §4.3 points to that section of the specification.

## 1. Objective

At every event of an AI coding agent's session, the model classifies the pattern of the agent's most recent eight operations as one of four classes:

1. **PRODUCTIVE**: evidence of forward progress or materially new investigation.
2. **RECOVERY**: a bounded retry or repair after a transient or diagnosed failure, still within policy or recently resolved.
3. **STALLED**: repeated ineffective operations, with no observed progress and no state-reversion cycle.
4. **OSCILLATING**: recurring reversal between previously held workspace or execution states, with no net progress.

The model reads the session's rendered log. No hand-written feature extractor sits between the log and the network. There is only a fixed renderer (§4) and a fixed tokeniser (§5).

### 1.2 What a good result does and does not show

- **The logs are synthetic, in one fixed grammar.** There is one header line per tool call, with a family-specific tool name and canonical result syntax. Tool output and assistant text are absent, and diff content is replaced by opaque hunk ids. A good score shows hand-programmed perception over this grammar. It does not show robustness to real transcripts.
- **Segmentation is given, not perceived.** `EOE` tokens, the `event_ord` input and an attention bias indexed by event distance make "same event" and "within the last 8 events" one scalar table each. This mirrors transcripts where each tool call is a record. It is a task-aligned inductive bias, and it computes no content signal.
- **The tokeniser is fixed and word-level.** Paths and identifiers are single tokens, and numbers are digit groups. It computes no repeat, state or delta signal.
- **Diff hunks are opaque ids.** Whether an edit repeats, undoes or restores an earlier change is visible. Whether it is correct code is not. In the real world, progress shows only through later validation, and that is the case here too.
- v0.3 makes no claim that hand-programming beats training.

## 6. Windows, gate, labels

- **Oracle rules.** The labels come from the v0.2 oracle. Its §6.1–§6.3 (latent state definitions, parameters, rules) and the family names in its §7.1 follow.
- **Gate rule.** Windows with withheld observations are not scored.

## v0.2 oracle rules and scenario families (unchanged in v0.3)

The labels are produced by the v0.2 oracle from the simulator's latent state. Its definitions,
parameters and rules (v0.2 §6.1-§6.3) and the names of the scenario families (v0.2 §7.1) are
reproduced here. "Encoded features" and "the 120-vector" refer to v0.2's input, which v0.3
replaces with the rendered log.

#### 6.1 Latent state (simulator-internal, never encoded)

Per session the simulator maintains:

- `progress p_t ∈ [0, 1]`: hidden objective completion.
- `knowledge K_t`: a set of latent facts about the fault. An operation may add facts. A new fact is "material narrowing".
- `workspace W_t`: real simulated file contents. Digests are computed from these.
- `episodes`: failure episodes with latent cause (`transient`, `persistent`, `diagnosed_repair`), a retry counter and a resolution flag.
- Per-operation latent effect: one of `PROGRESS`, `NEW_FACT`, `RESOLVES_EPISODE`, `IN_POLICY_RETRY`, `IN_POLICY_POLL`, `REVERSION`, `REDUNDANT`, `NONE`.

`REDUNDANT` means the operation repeats work already reflected in latent state. It re-acquires a fact already in `K_t`, re-applies an edit already present in `W_t`, re-runs validation on an unchanged workspace, or is an out-of-policy retry or poll. Redundancy is defined against `K_t` and `W_t`, **not** against `intent_fingerprint`, so it stays independent of the encoded features. `NONE` means the operation is novel but yielded nothing, for example a first read of a file that turns out to be irrelevant.

An episode's **initial failing operation** has effect `NONE`, because the attempt itself was reasonable. Its in-policy retries are `IN_POLICY_RETRY`. Retries beyond `R_max` are `REDUNDANT`.

An operation is **stall-ineffective** iff its latent effect is `REDUNDANT` or `REVERSION`. An operation is **ineffective** iff it is stall-ineffective or has effect `NONE`.

A **reversion** is an agent mutation whose latent after-state equals a workspace state held earlier in the window **and** that undoes an earlier agent mutation. External resets don't count.

#### 6.2 Pre-registered oracle parameters

| Symbol | Value | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `ε_p` | 0.02 | Progress tolerance over a window |
| `F_prod` | 2 | Minimum new facts in the window for investigative PRODUCTIVE |
| `N_stall` | 5 | Minimum ineffective operations of 8 for STALLED |
| `N_grey` | 3 | Lower bound of the stall grey zone |
| `N_rev` | 2 | Minimum reversions in the window for OSCILLATING |
| `R_max` | 3 | Maximum retries of one intent within an episode while still in policy |
| `P_max` | 5 | Maximum polls of an external dependency (with backoff) while still in policy |
| `k_rec` | 4 | Recency horizon for RECOVERY |

#### 6.3 Window labelling rules (evaluated in order; first match wins)

Let `Δp` be the progress change across the window, `F` the number of new facts, `I` the number of **stall-ineffective** operations (`REDUNDANT` + `REVERSION`) and `V` the number of reversions.

1. **INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (instrumentation):** the generator deliberately dropped a required observation (scenario 12).
2. **OSCILLATING:** `V ≥ N_rev` and `Δp ≤ ε_p`.
3. **STALLED:** `Δp ≤ ε_p`, `F = 0`, `I ≥ N_stall`, the final event is stall-ineffective, **and** no episode is in policy at the endpoint.
4. **RECOVERY:** an episode is active at the endpoint with retries ≤ `R_max` (or polls ≤ `P_max`), **or** an episode resolved within the last `k_rec` events.
5. **PRODUCTIVE:** `Δp > ε_p` or `F ≥ F_prod`.
6. **INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (ambiguous):** everything else. This includes the grey zone `N_grey ≤ I < N_stall` with no progress, windows with a single new fact and no progress, and aimless novel activity (mostly `NONE` effects). Novel but fruitless exploration is never labelled STALLED. Repetition of already-done work is what defines a stall.

This ordering gives `OSCILLATING > STALLED > RECOVERY > PRODUCTIVE`. The recency bound in rule 4 stops a long-resolved retry from overriding later productive work.

Labels depend on latent causal state. Observable features are emitted independently by the event layer. Labels are never defined in terms of encoded features. For example, there must be no rule of the form "STALLED iff `repeated_intent`".

#### 7.1 Scenario families (names only)

1. Incremental productive repair: failing tests, targeted edits, fewer failures, eventually green.
2. Productive exploration: several inspections and diagnostics before a meaningful change.
3. Transient external failure: repeated timeout, then success, then productive work.
4. Bounded backoff or retry: a recoverable failure with one or two controlled retries.
5. Repeated failed test invocation with unchanged artefact and unchanged failure.
6. Repeated edits that change files but don't improve validation.
7. A/B/A/B workspace oscillation between competing edits.
8. Tool oscillation: two operations repeatedly undo each other's effects.
9. Benign lookalike: repeated test runs with genuine incremental improvement.
10. Benign lookalike: repeated reads or polls while an external dependency legitimately recovers.
11. Rising context or token expenditure without useful work. Cost is weak supporting evidence, not a label shortcut.
12. Under-instrumented sessions, for gate coverage.

THE LOGS (the network's input): each session is rendered by renderer.py into one text block per event and tokenised by tokenizer.py (encode_session); the network reads the token ids, with each token's event ordinal and offset. Below: the specification's rendering and tokeniser sections, the id of every fixed token, the records the renderer reads, the exact source of renderer.py and tokenizer.py, and a grammar sheet with one invented example block per tool and its tokens.

## 4. Log rendering (frozen)

### 4.1 Layout

The log is `BOS`, then one **event block** per event in order. Each block is a header line plus up to 6 body lines, all ASCII (non-ASCII characters become `?` before any marker is inserted). The truncation marker is the ASCII word `TRUNC`.

### 4.2 Header line

```
{HH:MM:SS.mmm} {tool} {fields…} -> {status} in={input_tokens} out={output_tokens}
```

| Tool | Fields (budget in tokens) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `read_file` | `path={p}` [`lines={a}-{b}`] | `ok` / `error` |
| `search` | `scope={s} query="{q}"` (query ≤ 12) [`limit={n}`] | `ok` |
| `list_dir` | `path={p}` | `ok` |
| `edit_file` | `path={p}` | `ok` / `error` |
| `write_file` | `path={p}` | `ok` / `error` |
| `revert` | `paths={p1},{p2}…` (≤ 16) | `ok` |
| `run_tests` | `suite={s}` [`tests={t1},{t2}…`] (≤ 24) | `ok` or `FAILED` |
| `build`, `lint` | `target={t}` (`?` if the suite was dropped) | `ok` or `FAILED` |
| `http_call` | `{METHOD} https://{host}{path_template}` [`body={json}`] (body ≤ 16) `req={hex8}` | `ok` / `error` |
| `poll_status` | `resource={r}` [`backoff={b}`] | `ready` / `pending` |
| `plan`, `ask`, `yield` | `action={action_type}` | `ok` |

- **Validation counts.** For any event with a validation result, the status is followed by `{passed}/{total} passed`.
- **Field budgets.** A field over its budget is cut and ends with `TRUNC`.
- **The suffix is never cut.** The suffix is `-> {status} … in= out=`.
- **Header limit.** The whole header is at most 64 tokens, `TRUNC` included.

### 4.3 Body lines

These are emitted in this order, at most 6 lines in total:

1. **Hunk lines.** One line per changed file, in path order:
   ```
     @ {path} {h_old} > {h_new}
   ```
   - The diff is `difflib.unified_diff(before.split("\n"), after.split("\n"), n=0)`.
   - `h_x` is `h` plus the first 10 hex characters of `sha256(session_id + ":hunk:" + path + ":" + text)`, where `text` is the file's removed lines (for `h_old`) or added lines (for `h_new`), taken across all hunks in diff order and joined with `\n`.
   - An empty side renders as `h0`.
   - The same change in the same file and session always gets the same ids. An undo swaps them, and a return to earlier content reuses an earlier id.
   - The number of hunks inside a file is not shown. At most `min(5, 6 − tail lines)` file lines are shown. If more files changed, the last shown line is `  @ TRUNC {k}`, where `k` is the number of files not shown.
   - Hunk lines are still shown when workspace digests were dropped. Those windows are not scored, but later windows may refer back to them.
2. **Error line** (ERROR outcome only):
   ```
     ! {error_class} at {error_location}:{line} ({noise})
   ```
   - `{line}` is `int(sha256(session_id+":"+error_location)[:4],16) % 900 + 1`, so it is stable across repeats.
   - `{noise}` is `pid {n}` or `0x{hex8}`, drawn from the event's render RNG.
3. **Workspace line** (`[workspace untracked]`), emitted when either digest was dropped.

### 4.4 Missing observations

Each dropped field renders as `?` in its own position, for example `in=? out=812`, `?/18 passed`, `suite=?`, or `! ? at ?:? (…)` when the failure was dropped.

### 4.5 Noise

- **Render RNG.** Each event has its own render RNG, `random.Random(int(sha256(canonical_json(RawOp) + ":render")[:16], 16))`. It supplies `req=` and `{noise}`. It is independent of the generators and the oracle.
- **Timestamps.** These are parsed with `datetime.fromisoformat` and rendered in UTC as `HH:MM:SS.mmm`.

### 4.6 Bound

A block has at most 64 header tokens, then for each of up to 6 body lines one line-marker token plus at most 20 tokens, then `EOE`. That is at most 64 + 6·21 + 1 = 191 < `O`. The renderer enforces the per-line cap with `TRUNC`.

## 5. Tokeniser (frozen)

A deterministic left-to-right scan of each block. Spaces and tabs are dropped.

| Rule | Token |
|---|---|
| A newline followed (after spaces) by `@`, `!` or `[` | one reserved line-marker id `NL@`, `NL!` or `NL[` (the character is consumed) |
| Any other newline | `NL` |
| `WORD = [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.\-/]*` | one token: a reserved id if the word is reserved, otherwise a hashed id |
| `NUM = [0-9]+` | split left to right into groups of 3 digits (the last group may be shorter); each group is a dedicated id |
| Any other printable character | one punctuation id |

**Vocabulary (V = 10,240):**

| Ids | Content |
|---|---|
| 0 | `PAD` |
| 1 | `BOS` |
| 2 | `EOE` |
| 3 | `NL` |
| 4–6 | `NL@`, `NL!`, `NL[` |
| 7–127 | reserved words, frozen in `tokenizer.py`: all tool names; the words `path lines scope query limit bytes paths suite tests target body req resource backoff action in out ok error FAILED passed ready pending at pid workspace untracked TRUNC https GET POST PUT PATCH DELETE` |
| 128–223 | printable ASCII punctuation |
| 224–1,333 | digit groups `0`–`9`, `00`–`99`, `000`–`999` |
| 1,334–2,047 | unused |
| 2,048–10,239 | other words: `2048 + int(sha256(word)[:8],16) mod 8192` |

The tokeniser returns `tokens`, `event_ord`, `offset`, the indices of the `EOE` tokens, and the **surface strings** (each token's text before hashing).

Token ids (the tables of tokenizer.py, listed):
Special and line-marker tokens:
  0 PAD (padding only; never produced)   1 BOS   2 EOE   3 NL   4 NL@   5 NL!   6 NL[
Reserved words (ids 7-54; ids 55-127 are never produced):
  7 read_file   8 search   9 list_dir   10 edit_file   11 write_file   12 revert   13 run_tests
  14 build   15 lint   16 http_call   17 poll_status   18 plan   19 ask   20 yield
  21 path   22 lines   23 scope   24 query   25 limit   26 bytes   27 paths
  28 suite   29 tests   30 target   31 body   32 req   33 resource   34 backoff
  35 action   36 in   37 out   38 ok   39 error   40 FAILED   41 passed
  42 ready   43 pending   44 at   45 pid   46 workspace   47 untracked   48 TRUNC
  49 https   50 GET   51 POST   52 PUT   53 PATCH   54 DELETE
Punctuation (ids 128-158; ids 159-223 are never produced):
  128 !   129 "   130 #   131 $   132 %   133 &   134 '   135 (
  136 )   137 *   138 +   139 ,   140 -   141 .   142 /   143 :
  144 ;   145 <   146 =   147 >   148 ?   149 @   150 [   151 \
  152 ]   153 ^   154 `   155 {   156 |   157 }   158 ~
Digit groups (a number is split left to right into groups of 3 digits; the last group may be shorter):
  a 1-digit group g ("0".."9") has id 224 + g (224-233); a 2-digit group ("00".."99") has id 234 + its value
  (234-333); a 3-digit group ("000".."999") has id 334 + its value (334-1333). For example "09" is 243 and
  "250" is 584. Ids 1334-2047 are never produced.
Every other word: id 2048 + (int(sha256(word)[:8], 16) mod 8192), in 2048-10239.

## Operation records (`RawOp` dicts, the renderer's input)

`renderer.render_session(ops, session_id)` returns one block string per operation; `ops` is a list
of plain dicts, one per tool call, with these keys (a missing key reads as null; `session_id` is any
string, and it seeds the hunk ids and error line numbers of §4.3):

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `family` | str | The tool name: `read_file`, `search`, `list_dir`, `edit_file`, `write_file`, `revert`, `run_tests`, `build`, `lint`, `http_call`, `poll_status`, `plan`, `ask`, `yield` |
| `target` | str, list or dict | What the call acts on: the path (`read_file`, `list_dir`, `edit_file`, `write_file`), the scope (`search`), the list of paths (`revert`), the suite (`run_tests`), the target (`build`, `lint`), `{"method", "host", "path_template"}` (`http_call`), the resource (`poll_status`) |
| `args` | dict | Call arguments the header shows: `line_start` / `line_end` (`read_file`), `content` (`write_file`; not shown in the header), `query` / `limit` (`search`), `tests` (a list, `run_tests`), `body` (`http_call`), `backoff` (`poll_status`), `action_type` (`plan`, `ask`, `yield`) |
| `outcome` | str | `SUCCESS`, `ERROR` or `NEUTRAL`. The status reads `error` for `ERROR` and `ok` otherwise; `run_tests` / `build` / `lint` read `FAILED` / `ok`, and `poll_status` reads `ready` / `error` / `pending` |
| `error_class`, `error_location` | str or null | The error line of an `ERROR` outcome: `! {error_class} at {error_location}:{line} (...)` |
| `validation` | `{"suite", "passed", "total"}` or null | The validation result; shown as `{passed}/{total} passed` |
| `changed` | list of `{"path", "before", "after"}` | Every tracked file whose text differs between the start and the end of the call, sorted by path; `before` / `after` is the full text, or null when the file is absent. Rendered as hunk lines (§4.3) |
| `extra` | dict or null | Tool-specific detail that the header does not show |
| `input_tokens`, `output_tokens` | int or null | Shown as `in=` and `out=` |
| `timestamp` | str or null | ISO 8601 (`2026-03-01T09:14:03.250+00:00`); shown in UTC as `HH:MM:SS.mmm` |
| `dropped` | sorted list of str | Observations withheld on this call, each shown as `?` in its own position: any of `digest_after`, `digest_before`, `failure`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `validation_passed`, `validation_suite`, `validation_total` (a dropped digest adds the `[workspace untracked]` line) |

The renderer's exact source (renderer.py):

```python
"""v0.3 log renderer (spec v0.3 §4). Frozen; ships in the authoring packet.

Standalone: standard library only, plus the sibling packet module ``tokenizer`` (imported lazily so
the harness can also import this file as ``agent_loop_lab.v03.renderer``).

    blocks = render_session(rawops, session_id)   # rawops: list of RawOp dicts (RawOp.to_dict())

One block per event: a header line, then at most 6 body lines (hunk lines, error line, workspace line).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import difflib
import hashlib
import json
import random
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, Mapping, Sequence

try:  # packet layout: tokenizer.py next to this file
    import tokenizer as _tok  # type: ignore
except ImportError:  # harness layout
    from . import tokenizer as _tok  # type: ignore

HEADER_MAX_TOKENS = 64
BODY_MAX_LINES = 6
LINE_MAX_TOKENS = 20  # excluding the line-marker token
HUNK_MAX_LINES = 5
TRUNC = "TRUNC"

FIELD_BUDGETS = {"tests": 24, "body": 16, "paths": 16, "query": 12}

VALIDATE_FAMILIES = ("run_tests", "build", "lint")
DIGEST_DROPS = ("digest_before", "digest_after")


def _get(op: Mapping[str, Any] | Any, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
    if isinstance(op, Mapping):
        return op.get(key, default)
    return getattr(op, key, default)


def _ascii(text: str) -> str:
    return "".join(ch if 32 <= ord(ch) < 127 else "?" for ch in str(text))


def _ntok(text: str) -> int:
    return len(_tok.tokenize_block(text))


def _fit(text: str, budget: int) -> str:
    """ASCII-sanitise ``text`` and cut it to at most ``budget`` tokens, ending with TRUNC when cut.

    The cut keeps the source text up to the end of the last kept token, so the kept part reads
    exactly as it would uncut; a space before TRUNC keeps it a separate word."""
    text = _ascii(text)
    spans = _tok.tokenize_spans(text)
    if len(spans) <= budget:
        return text
    keep = max(0, budget - 1)
    kept = text[: spans[keep - 1][3]] if keep else ""
    return (kept + " " + TRUNC) if kept else TRUNC


def canonical_json(obj: Any) -> str:
    return json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True, default=str)


def render_rng(op: Mapping[str, Any] | Any) -> random.Random:
    d = op if isinstance(op, Mapping) else op.to_dict()
    seed = int(hashlib.sha256((canonical_json(d) + ":render").encode()).hexdigest()[:16], 16)
    return random.Random(seed)


def _clock(ts: str | None) -> str:
    if not ts:
        return "?"
    t = datetime.fromisoformat(ts)
    if t.tzinfo is not None:
        t = t.astimezone(timezone.utc)
    return f"{t:%H:%M:%S}.{t.microsecond // 1000:03d}"


def _q(v: Any) -> str:
    return "?" if v is None else str(v)


def hunk_id(session_id: str, path: str, lines: Sequence[str]) -> str:
    if not lines:
        return "h0"
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    return "h" + hashlib.sha256(f"{session_id}:hunk:{path}:{text}".encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:10]


def diff_hunks(before: str | None, after: str | None) -> list[tuple[list[str], list[str]]]:
    """(removed lines, added lines) per hunk of the n=0 unified diff."""
    a = [] if before is None else before.split("\n")
    b = [] if after is None else after.split("\n")
    lines = list(difflib.unified_diff(a, b, "a", "b", lineterm="", n=0))[2:]
    hunks: list[tuple[list[str], list[str]]] = []
    for ln in lines:
        if ln.startswith("@@"):
            hunks.append(([], []))
        elif hunks and ln.startswith("-"):
            hunks[-1][0].append(ln[1:])
        elif hunks and ln.startswith("+"):
            hunks[-1][1].append(ln[1:])
    return hunks


def _status(op: Any) -> str:
    family, outcome = _get(op, "family"), _get(op, "outcome")
    dropped = set(_get(op, "dropped") or ())
    val = _get(op, "validation")
    if family == "poll_status":
        status = "ready" if outcome == "SUCCESS" else ("pending" if outcome == "NEUTRAL" else "error")
    elif family in VALIDATE_FAMILIES:
        status = "FAILED" if outcome == "ERROR" else "ok"
    else:
        status = "error" if outcome == "ERROR" else "ok"
    if val is not None:
        p = "?" if "validation_passed" in dropped else _q(val.get("passed"))
        t = "?" if "validation_total" in dropped else _q(val.get("total"))
        status += f" {p}/{t} passed"
    tin = "?" if "input_tokens" in dropped else _q(_get(op, "input_tokens"))
    tout = "?" if "output_tokens" in dropped else _q(_get(op, "output_tokens"))
    return f"-> {status} in={tin} out={tout}"


def _fields(op: Any, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    family = _get(op, "family")
    target = _get(op, "target")
    args = _get(op, "args") or {}
    dropped = set(_get(op, "dropped") or ())
    parts: list[str] = []
    if family in ("read_file", "list_dir", "edit_file"):
        parts.append(f"path={target}")
        if family == "read_file" and (args.get("line_start") is not None or args.get("line_end") is not None):
            parts.append(f"lines={_q(args.get('line_start'))}-{_q(args.get('line_end'))}")
    elif family == "write_file":
        parts.append(f"path={target}")
    elif family == "search":
        parts.append(f"scope={target}")
        parts.append('query="' + _fit(str(args.get("query", "")), FIELD_BUDGETS["query"]) + '"')
        if args.get("limit") is not None:
            parts.append(f"limit={args['limit']}")
    elif family == "revert":
        paths = target if isinstance(target, (list, tuple)) else [target]
        parts.append("paths=" + _fit(",".join(str(p) for p in paths), FIELD_BUDGETS["paths"]))
    elif family == "run_tests":
        suite = "?" if "validation_suite" in dropped else target
        parts.append(f"suite={suite}")
        if args.get("tests"):
            parts.append("tests=" + _fit(",".join(str(t) for t in args["tests"]), FIELD_BUDGETS["tests"]))
    elif family in ("build", "lint"):
        suite_dropped = "validation_suite" in dropped and _get(op, "validation") is not None
        parts.append(f"target={'?' if suite_dropped else target}")
    elif family == "http_call":
        t = target or {}
        parts.append(f"{t.get('method', '?')} https://{t.get('host', '?')}{t.get('path_template', '')}")
        if args.get("body") is not None:
            parts.append("body=" + _fit(str(args["body"]), FIELD_BUDGETS["body"]))
        parts.append(f"req={rng.getrandbits(32):08x}")
    elif family == "poll_status":
        parts.append(f"resource={target}")
        if args.get("backoff") is not None:
            parts.append(f"backoff={args['backoff']}")
    elif family in ("plan", "ask", "yield"):
        parts.append(f"action={args.get('action_type', '?')}")
    else:
        parts.append(f"target={target}")
    return " ".join(parts)


def _header(op: Any, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    head = f"{_clock(_get(op, 'timestamp'))} {_get(op, 'family')}"
    suffix = _status(op)
    fields = _ascii(_fields(op, rng))
    room = HEADER_MAX_TOKENS - _ntok(head) - _ntok(suffix)
    if _ntok(fields) > room:
        fields = _fit(fields, room)
    return _ascii(f"{head} {fields} {suffix}")


def _line(marker: str, text: str) -> str:
    return "  " + marker + " " + _fit(_ascii(text), LINE_MAX_TOKENS)


def render_event(op: Any, session_id: str) -> str:
    rng = render_rng(op)
    header = _header(op, rng)
    hunk_lines: list[str] = []
    for ch in sorted(_get(op, "changed") or [], key=lambda c: c["path"]):
        # One line per changed file (spec v0.3 r2 §4.3): all removed lines vs all added lines of the
        # n=0 diff, so the number of hunks inside a file is not shown.
        hunks = diff_hunks(ch.get("before"), ch.get("after"))
        if not hunks:
            continue
        removed = [ln for r, _ in hunks for ln in r]
        added = [ln for _, a in hunks for ln in a]
        path = ch["path"]
        hunk_lines.append(f"{path} {hunk_id(session_id, path, removed)} > {hunk_id(session_id, path, added)}")
    tail: list[str] = []
    if _get(op, "outcome") == "ERROR":
        dropped = set(_get(op, "dropped") or ())
        loc = _get(op, "error_location")
        if "failure" in dropped:
            cls, loc_s, line = "?", "?", "?"
        else:
            cls = _q(_get(op, "error_class"))
            loc_s = _q(loc)
            line = "?" if loc is None else str(int(hashlib.sha256(f"{session_id}:{loc}".encode()).hexdigest()[:4], 16) % 900 + 1)
        noise = f"pid {rng.randint(1000, 99999)}" if rng.random() < 0.5 else f"0x{rng.getrandbits(32):08x}"
        tail.append(("!", f"{cls} at {loc_s}:{line} ({noise})"))
    if set(_get(op, "dropped") or ()) & set(DIGEST_DROPS):
        tail.append(("[", "workspace untracked]"))
    max_hunks = min(HUNK_MAX_LINES, BODY_MAX_LINES - len(tail))
    if len(hunk_lines) > max_hunks:
        omitted = len(hunk_lines) - (max_hunks - 1)
        hunk_lines = hunk_lines[: max_hunks - 1] + [f"{TRUNC} {omitted}"]
    body = [_line("@", h) for h in hunk_lines] + [_line(m, t) for m, t in tail]
    return "\n".join([header] + body)


def render_session(rawops: Sequence[Any], session_id: str) -> list[str]:
    return [render_event(op, session_id) for op in rawops]
```

The tokeniser's exact source (tokenizer.py):

```python
"""v0.3 tokeniser (spec v0.3 §5). Frozen; ships in the authoring packet.

Standalone: standard library only, no relative imports.

    enc = encode_session(blocks)   # blocks: one rendered string per event (renderer.render_session)
    enc.tokens, enc.event_ord, enc.offset, enc.eoe_index, enc.surface

A session is ``BOS`` followed, for each event block, by the block's tokens and then ``EOE``.
``event_ord`` is 0 for ``BOS`` and k+1 for every token of block k, including its ``EOE``.
``offset`` is the 0-based position within the block (``BOS`` has offset 0); an offset >= ``O`` raises.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

V = 10240
O = 192

PAD, BOS, EOE, NL = 0, 1, 2, 3
NL_AT, NL_BANG, NL_BRACKET = 4, 5, 6
LINE_MARKERS = {"@": NL_AT, "!": NL_BANG, "[": NL_BRACKET}

TOOL_NAMES = (
    "read_file", "search", "list_dir", "edit_file", "write_file", "revert", "run_tests", "build", "lint",
    "http_call", "poll_status", "plan", "ask", "yield",
)
FIELD_AND_STATUS_WORDS = (
    "path", "lines", "scope", "query", "limit", "bytes", "paths", "suite", "tests", "target", "body", "req",
    "resource", "backoff", "action", "in", "out", "ok", "error", "FAILED", "passed", "ready", "pending", "at",
    "pid", "workspace", "untracked", "TRUNC", "https", "GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE",
)
RESERVED_WORDS: tuple[str, ...] = TOOL_NAMES + FIELD_AND_STATUS_WORDS
RESERVED_BASE = 7
assert RESERVED_BASE + len(RESERVED_WORDS) <= 128
RESERVED_IDS: dict[str, int] = {w: RESERVED_BASE + i for i, w in enumerate(RESERVED_WORDS)}

PUNCT_BASE = 128
PUNCT_CHARS = "".join(chr(c) for c in range(33, 127) if not chr(c).isalnum() and chr(c) != "_")
assert len(PUNCT_CHARS) <= 96
PUNCT_IDS: dict[str, int] = {ch: PUNCT_BASE + i for i, ch in enumerate(PUNCT_CHARS)}

DIGIT_BASE = 224
DIGIT_GROUPS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    tuple(f"{i}" for i in range(10)) + tuple(f"{i:02d}" for i in range(100)) + tuple(f"{i:03d}" for i in range(1000))
)
DIGIT_IDS: dict[str, int] = {g: DIGIT_BASE + i for i, g in enumerate(DIGIT_GROUPS)}
assert DIGIT_BASE + len(DIGIT_GROUPS) == 1334

HASH_BASE = 2048
HASH_BUCKETS = 8192
assert HASH_BASE + HASH_BUCKETS == V

_WORD = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.\-/]*")
_NUM = re.compile(r"[0-9]+")


class TokenizerError(ValueError):
    pass


def word_id(word: str) -> int:
    """Id of a WORD token: reserved id if reserved, otherwise its hashed bucket."""
    if word in RESERVED_IDS:
        return RESERVED_IDS[word]
    return HASH_BASE + int(hashlib.sha256(word.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8], 16) % HASH_BUCKETS


def digit_groups(num: str) -> list[str]:
    """Split a digit string left to right into groups of 3 (the last may be shorter)."""
    return [num[i : i + 3] for i in range(0, len(num), 3)]


def tokenize_spans(block: str) -> list[tuple[int, str, int, int]]:
    """(id, surface, start, end) per token of one event block (without EOE); ``block[start:end]`` is the
    matched source text (for a line marker, the newline, any spaces and the marker character)."""
    out: list[tuple[int, str, int, int]] = []
    i, n = 0, len(block)
    while i < n:
        ch = block[i]
        if ch in " \t":
            i += 1
            continue
        if ch == "\n":
            j = i + 1
            while j < n and block[j] in " \t":
                j += 1
            if j < n and block[j] in LINE_MARKERS:
                out.append((LINE_MARKERS[block[j]], "\n" + block[j], i, j + 1))
                i = j + 1
            else:
                out.append((NL, "\n", i, i + 1))
                i += 1
            continue
        m = _WORD.match(block, i)
        if m:
            w = m.group(0)
            out.append((word_id(w), w, i, m.end()))
            i = m.end()
            continue
        m = _NUM.match(block, i)
        if m:
            for k, g in enumerate(digit_groups(m.group(0))):
                out.append((DIGIT_IDS[g], g, i + 3 * k, i + 3 * k + len(g)))
            i = m.end()
            continue
        if ch in PUNCT_IDS:
            out.append((PUNCT_IDS[ch], ch, i, i + 1))
            i += 1
            continue
        raise TokenizerError(f"unrenderable character {ch!r} at {i}")
    return out


def tokenize_block(block: str) -> list[tuple[int, str]]:
    """(id, surface) pairs for one event block (without EOE)."""
    return [(tid, s) for tid, s, _, _ in tokenize_spans(block)]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Encoded:
    tokens: list[int]
    event_ord: list[int]
    offset: list[int]
    eoe_index: list[int]
    surface: list[str]


def encode_session(blocks: list[str]) -> Encoded:
    tokens, event_ord, offset, eoe, surface = [BOS], [0], [0], [], ["<BOS>"]
    for k, block in enumerate(blocks):
        pairs = tokenize_block(block)
        pairs.append((EOE, "<EOE>"))
        if len(pairs) > O:
            raise TokenizerError(f"event block {k} has {len(pairs)} tokens (offset >= O={O})")
        for off, (tid, s) in enumerate(pairs):
            tokens.append(tid)
            event_ord.append(k + 1)
            offset.append(off)
            surface.append(s)
        eoe.append(len(tokens) - 1)
    return Encoded(tokens, event_ord, offset, eoe, surface)


def prefix(enc: Encoded, t: int) -> Encoded:
    """The encoding of blocks 0..t (inclusive): a prefix ending at EOE_t."""
    end = enc.eoe_index[t] + 1
    return Encoded(enc.tokens[:end], enc.event_ord[:end], enc.offset[:end], enc.eoe_index[: t + 1], enc.surface[:end])
```

# Grammar sheet (spec v0.3 §4-§5)

Each example below is one **event block** as the frozen renderer lays it out, followed by its
tokens from the frozen tokenizer (`tokenizer.tokenize_block`, then `EOE`), one per line as
`offset  id  surface`. Line-marker tokens are shown as `NL@`, `NL!` and `NL[`.

Every path, suite, test, target, host, action, error class, hunk id and number here is
**invented** for illustration. Real logs use the same grammar with other values.

A session is `BOS` followed by its blocks in order (`tokenizer.encode_session`). `event_ord` is 0
for `BOS` and k+1 for every token of block k, including its `EOE`; `offset` restarts at 0 in every
block. The network's prediction for block k is read at that block's `EOE`.

Header suffix: `-> {status}[ {passed}/{total} passed] in={input_tokens} out={output_tokens}`.
Body lines, at most 6, in this order: hunk lines (`@`, at most 5), the error line (`!`, ERROR
outcomes only) and the workspace line (`[`, when a digest was dropped). A dropped observation is
rendered as `?` in its own position.

1	# CIRCUITS.md — the revised network (r1's weights + `REVISION.edits`)
2	
3	This describes the network the harness builds from `r1/artifact.dlw` with `REVISION.edits` applied. Section
4	numbering of the statements refers to the `# ====` section letters inside `REVISION.edits` (A–J). "r1" means
5	the weights r1 wrote; "kept" means the block is r1's and unchanged; "changed"/"new" means this revision
6	wrote it. Dimension `dN` is residual dimension N. `clip(x)` means `relu(x) − relu(x − 1)` (two MLP units
7	with biases differing by 1 and output weights +1/−1), which maps any pre-activation to [0, 1].
8	
9	The decision the network implements (the oracle's rule order, with observable proxies):
10	
11	```
12	OSCILLATING  if  at least 2 reverting mutations among the last 8 events
13	else RECOVERY if  the most recent outcome event in the last 8 is an in-policy retry (act)
14	else STALLED  if  at least 5 of the last 8 events are ineffective AND the current event is ineffective
15	else RECOVERY if  a resolution happened in the last 4 events (resw)
16	else PRODUCTIVE
17	```
18	
19	Logits: `PRODUCTIVE = 0.5`, `RECOVERY = 8·act + 5·resw − 2`, `STALLED = 6·sc + 6·INEFF_t − 8·act − 8`,
20	`OSCILLATING = 12·osc`.

93	## 4. Layer 1 attention: code matching (all heads: distance 0 → −10000)
94	
95	Scores are q·k/4. A one-hot code with 3 ones (A) gives 32·3/4 = 24 for a full match, 16 for 2 of 3; a code
96	B (2 ones) gives 16 / 8. Because keys are role-signed, a query from one role scores negatively against the
97	other role's keys of the same block and never attends to them.
98	
99	| head | q from | k from | range (bias 0) | BOS | v → o | output meaning |
100	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
101	| 0 | 32·d32–47 | d64–79 | 1..7 | 20 | ⅓Σd64–79 → d116 | REVtokA: a hunk id whose code A matched a hunk id of the last 7 events (kept) |

104	| 3 | 32·d64–79 | d64–79 | 1..2 | 20 | ⅓Σd64–79 → d119 | at a line digit: −0.98 if the same line occurred in the previous 2 events (D3) |

106	| 5 | 32·d96–111 | d96–111 | 1..31 | 24 | ⅓Σd96–111 → d113 | +k/(k+1) at a count digit (earlier equal counts), −k/(k+1) at a poll resource (earlier polls) (D5) |

111	the BOS and the k matching keys, so the value is k/(k+1): 0.5, 0.667, 0.75, 0.8, 0.833, 0.857 for k = 1..6.

# CIRCUITS.md — the revised network (r1's weights + `REVISION.edits`)

This describes the network the harness builds from `r1/artifact.dlw` with `REVISION.edits` applied. Section
numbering of the statements refers to the `# ====` section letters inside `REVISION.edits` (A–J). "r1" means
the weights r1 wrote; "kept" means the block is r1's and unchanged; "changed"/"new" means this revision
wrote it. Dimension `dN` is residual dimension N. `clip(x)` means `relu(x) − relu(x − 1)` (two MLP units
with biases differing by 1 and output weights +1/−1), which maps any pre-activation to [0, 1].

The decision the network implements (the oracle's rule order, with observable proxies):

```
OSCILLATING  if  at least 2 reverting mutations among the last 8 events
else RECOVERY if  the most recent outcome event in the last 8 is an in-policy retry (act)
else STALLED  if  at least 5 of the last 8 events are ineffective AND the current event is ineffective
else RECOVERY if  a resolution happened in the last 4 events (resw)
else PRODUCTIVE
```

Logits: `PRODUCTIVE = 0.5`, `RECOVERY = 8·act + 5·resw − 2`, `STALLED = 6·sc + 6·INEFF_t − 8·act − 8`,
`OSCILLATING = 12·osc`.

## 1. Residual-subspace allocation (128 dims)

| dims | content | written by |
|---|---|---|
| d0 | constant 1 (every token) | embedding (kept) |
| d1 | hashed word (ids 2048+) and the token `.` (id 141) | embedding (kept + A7) |
| d2 | digit group | embedding (kept) |
| d3 `>`, d4 `NL@`, d5 `EOE` | token flags | embedding (kept) |
| d6 read_file/list_dir, d7 search, d8 edit/write/revert, d11 build/lint, d12 run_tests, d13 poll_status, d16 http_call, d18 plan/ask/yield | tool-class flags on the tool token; layer-0 head 2 adds the same flag to every later token of the event (value 1 there, 2 on the tool token itself) | embedding (d6–d8 kept, others A3–A6) + layer-0 attention |
| d9 `:` flag, d10 ok/ready flag, d14 error, d15 FAILED, d17 pending | status/punctuation token flags | embedding (A1, A2; d14/15/17 kept) |
| d19 offset o, d20 o², d21 o=7, d22 o=10, d23 o=14 | offset features | offset embedding (kept) |
| d24 prev1 is `:`, d25 prev1 is `>`, d26 prev2 is `>`, d27 prev2 is `NL@` | previous-token copies | layer-0 heads 0/1 (d25, d27 kept; d24, d26 new) |
| d28 FAILED, d29 ok/ready, d114 error, d115 pending | status broadcast: the event's status word, visible at every token after it | layer-0 head 4 (new) |
| d31 | hunk-line count k/(k+1) with a BOS sink | layer-0 head 3 (kept) |
| d32–47 | code A (one-hot of id mod 4, 5, 7) of hashed/digit tokens; **block 3**: targets (read/list path, search word, plan action, build/lint target) carry 2× the code after layer-0 MLP | embedding (kept) + layer-0 MLP |
| d48–63 | code B (one-hot of id mod 3, 13) in the embedding, cancelled by layer-0 MLP; **block 3 B**: code B at targets only; cancelled again by layer-1 MLP, then layer-1 flags: d48 (0), d49 NOOP, d50 HTTPERR, d51 POLLPEND, d52 SAMEFAILED, d53 outcome, d54 kpen, d55 hascount, d56 is_key, d57 POLL2g, d58 muthunk | embedding, layer-0 MLP, layer-1 MLP |
| d64–79 | **block 1 A**: role-signed keys, +code A at hunk ids (h_old/h_new), −code A at error-line digits; zeroed by layer-1 MLP; then layer-2/3 features d64 g_CNT2, d65 g_hascount, d66 g_REV, d67 g_REP, d68 g_POLL2, d69 prevmut, d70 r_HTTPERR, d71 r_POLLPEND, d72 r_SAMEF, d73 r_CNTOK, d74 kpen_ev, d75 INEFF, d76 RES, d77 INPOL, d79 A1, d80 A2, d81 act, d82 resw, d83 osc, d84 sc, d85 act_b, d86 resw_b | layer-0 MLP, layer-1 MLP, layers 2–3 |
| d80–95 | **block 1 B**: +code B at hunk ids, −code B at line digits; zeroed by layer-1 MLP (d80–86 reused as above) | layer-0 MLP |
| d96–111 | **block 2 A**: +code A at the passed-count digit, −code A at poll resources | layer-0 MLP |
| d59 g_SAME, d60 g_LINE2, d61 g_SAMEF, d62 KVev, d63 g_CNTOK | event-level gathers | layer-2 attention |
| d113 count-repeat / poll-count value, d116 REVtokA, d117 REVtokB, d118 line-count value, d119 LINE2 value, d120 CNT2/POLL2 value, d26 REP-A value, d9 REP-B value | layer-1 attention outputs (signed match values, see §4) | layer-1 attention |
| d121 REVg, d122 REPg, d123 CNTOKg, d124 SAMEg, d125 LINE2g, d126 CNT2g, d127 KV | token-level flags | layer-1 MLP |
| d30, d112, d78, d87–95 after layer 1, d96–111 after layer 1 | unused or dead | — |

Dead r1 dims: d30 (nothing writes it now), d112 (status_true; its unit is zeroed), d40 (r1's FNCev; its
head is cleared).

## 2. Embeddings

- `tok_emb` column 0: 1 for every id (kept). Column 1: ids 2048–10239 and 141 (A7). Column 2: digit groups
  224–1333 (kept). Columns 3, 4, 5: ids 147 (`>`), 4 (`NL@`), 2 (`EOE`) (kept). Columns 6, 7, 8: ids {7, 9},
  {8}, {10, 11, 12} (kept). Column 9: id 143 `:` (A1). Column 10: ids 38 `ok`, 42 `ready` (A2). Column 11:
  ids 14, 15 (A3). Column 12: id 13 (A4). Column 13: id 17; column 16: id 16 (A5). Columns 14, 15, 17: ids
  39, 40, 43 (kept). Column 18: ids 18, 19, 20 (A6).
- Columns 32–47 (code A: mod 4 → d32–35, mod 5 → d36–40, mod 7 → d41–47) for hashed ids and digit groups
  (kept) plus id 141 (d33, d37, d42; A7). Columns 48–63 (code B: mod 3 → d48–50, mod 13 → d51–63) for hashed
  ids (kept) plus id 141 (d48, d62; A7).
- `off_emb`: d19 = o, d20 = o², d21/22/23 = [o = 7/10/14] (kept).

## 3. Layer 0

### Attention (rel_bias rows 0, 1, 2, 4: 0 at distance 0, −10000 elsewhere incl. BOS; row 3: BOS +20)

| head | q (rows) | k | v → o | role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | rows 0–2 from d0, d19, d20: `q = (−64o² + 128o − 64, 128o − 128, −64)` (r1 ×2, B1) | rows 0–2 = (d0, d19, d20) (kept) | d3 → d25 (kept), d9 → d24 (B2) | exact copy of the previous token's `>` and `:` flags: score −16(o_i − 1 − o_j)² |

1	# REVISION.md — v05 Phase B revision of r1's network
2	
3	## 1. What was disclosed, and the base
4	
5	- Report: `disclosure/DISCLOSURE.json`, sha256
6	  `372a1c4209e9fc15b21b45375a3868ee53c0b04595e0bcdc0b84e3570c7e4677` (also in
7	  `disclosure/DISCLOSURE.sha256`): 200 validation windows V001–V200, 50 per oracle class, each with the
8	  rendered prefix (window marker at block t−7), the oracle label and r1's network's class at `EOE_t`. No
9	  reference-policy class exists (r1 wrote none). Nothing else was used: no other data, labels or metrics.
10	- Base: `r1/artifact.dlw`, sha256 `46d4b2a221dc0ecfb447d15b288ffb093d4612a9720cf87ed953221989ef56ac`
11	  (`./py -m v05_load r1` confirms the hash and that the frozen reader rebuilds it identically from
12	  `r1/replies/`).
13	- Deliverable: `REVISION.edits` (1262 statements, all applied, `./py -m v05_load check` reports that the
14	  harness would accept it). It was written by `scratch/gen_revision.py`, which only prints hand-chosen
15	  constants (the 16-dimensional one-hot code blocks are typed out by loops); no value in it comes from a
16	  search, a fit or an optimisation over the disclosed windows.
17	
18	On the 200 disclosed windows r1's network has macro-F1 0.331 (false-alarm rate 0.93); the revised network
19	has macro-F1 0.995 (V051 is the only disagreement). These numbers are a self-check on the disclosed report,
20	not an evaluation.
21	
22	## 2. Diagnosis of r1's network
23	
24	r1's design (tokens → gated code keys → cross-event code matching → per-event flags → window sums → ramps)
25	is sound and is kept. Its single fatal defect is in the layer-0 MLP "target code" units 32–63: the gate
26	`relu(codeA_d + hashed + offset + class − 2)` requires only two of the three conditions when the code bit
27	is 0, so at every read/list path and search word all 16 code dimensions fire (a key of sum 19 instead of a
28	3-hot code). Every later coded token then "matches" these keys (`MATCHtok ≈ 6.3` instead of ≤ 1), the
29	re-read and repeated-count flags fire on every token (`REPg ≈ 8.7`), and the per-event ineffectiveness
30	`INEFF` reaches ≈ 10, which gives STALLED logits of 60–90 on 141 of 200 windows (every PRODUCTIVE and
31	RECOVERY window of the report except V026, V052, V059, V095, V179, V187, V196, which r1 called
32	PRODUCTIVE — see the baseline in ITERATIONS.md iteration 0). Changing that one bias (`layers.0.mlp.fc1.bias[32:64] = -3`) alone lifts
33	the disclosed macro-F1 to 0.714 (iteration 2).
34	
35	The remaining errors after that fix come from r1's decision logic, which does not follow the oracle's
36	rules closely enough: STALLED needs the final event to be ineffective and r1 only counted re-runs with the
37	same failing count and re-reads within 7 events (V009, V119, V125, V172 end on repeats 10–18 events back;
38	V027, V040, V060, V063, V079, V091, V099, V104, V107, V116, V118, V139, V158 end on an edit of a
39	"change files but nothing improves" loop; V071, V145, V159 involve lints/builds); RECOVERY in r1 was "a
40	fail in the last 5 events and few fails overall", which fires on productive windows with a failed test or
41	a resolved http error (V003, V004, V017, V021, V022, V038, V059, V078, V080, V089, V094, V102, V108, V109,
42	V110) and misses resolutions and active retries (V088, V112, V137, V175, V181, V189, V197).
43	
44	## 3. The rules the revised network implements (and the windows behind them)
45	
46	All quantities are observable in the rendered log; thresholds are the oracle's parameters.
47	
48	1. **Reversion** (kept from r1): a hunk line whose `h_new` equals an earlier hunk id (`h_old` or `h_new`)
49	   of the last 7 events (both code A and code B). Two or more such mutations in the last 8 events →
50	   OSCILLATING. This was already right on 38 of 50 windows; the other 12 (V041, V050, V056, V057, V061, V070,
51	   V076, V081, V098, V121, V122, V161) were lost only to the inflated STALLED logit.
52	2. **Failure identity = the error-line number.** The rendered `{line}` is a stable hash of the full error
53	   location, so two failures with the same line are the same failure (V006, V013, V035, V062: same `:NNN`
54	   throughout; V003, V029: same test file but different tests, different lines). Count keys alone (r1) merge
55	   `FAILED 0/1` of different tests (V137, V181) and miss V062 (`4/11` then `0/1` ×4 at `:670`).
56	3. **Retry** = the same failure (same line, and the same passed count when there is one) within the previous
57	   2 events with no mutation in between (V088, V115, V154, V157, V174, V176, V185, V192, V197: retries;
58	   V029, V046, V097, V109: a focused re-run with a different count, not a retry; V037, V060, V062, V139,
59	   V147, V168: edits between the failures, not retries). For polls: the same resource within 2 events.
60	4. **In policy** = at most 3 earlier identical failures (`R_max = 3`; V154, V174, V176 have exactly 3 and
61	   are RECOVERY; V037, V062, V066 have 4+ and are STALLED), at most 5 earlier pending polls of the resource
62	   (`P_max = 5`; V030 ends on its sixth pending and is RECOVERY; V044, V163 go beyond and are STALLED).
63	5. **Active episode** (`act`) = the most recent outcome event (a failure, or an ok/ready of http/poll/
64	   validation) among the last 8 is an in-policy retry (V112, V149, V152, V173, V177, V178, V180, V183,
